external_sources.title: Spectral equivalence of matrix polynomials and the index sum theorem
external_sources.locator: Lemma 6.3, printed page 37 (PDF page 38 including cover); Remark 6.4
external_sources.imported_statement: For any square or rectangular matrix pencil over an arbitrary field, finite and infinite structural indices together with left and right minimal indices sum to its rational-function rank. Dropping the nonnegative structural indices gives the inequality used here.

external_sources.title: Another proof of Grothendieck's theorem on the splitting of vector bundles on the projective line
external_sources.locator: Theorem 2.1, PDF page 3; arbitrary-field setup on PDF page 2
external_sources.imported_statement: Every algebraic vector bundle on P1 over a field splits into line bundles. Applied to the basepoint-free evaluation kernel; H0(E)=0 forces its splitting degrees to be negative.
external_sources.read: Primary PDF, field setup and theorem statement re-opened in this generating session.

prior_credit: The cap, scalar Hankel description, pencil minimal-index argument, fixed-scheme reductions, Segre dimension estimates, polynomial source-rank inequality and ordinary-map application retain the credit of the pinned local and external sources. No historical-priority claim is made.
local_work: Extension to arbitrary characteristic by the divided-square (swap-invariant tensor) evaluation sequence, retaining separate diagonal equations in characteristic two; explicit geometric hypothesis over finite fields and audit of inherited field assumptions.
field_and_hypotheses: Any field K; 1<=r<min(a,b), 5r<2(a+b). Every (r+1)-minor of the Hankel image of the symbolic decomposable input must vanish identically, equivalently the rank bound holds on decomposable inputs over an algebraic closure. Rational-point rank testing alone over finite K is not assumed sufficient. Ordinary-map consequence uses actual tensor restriction identities over K.
limitations: No improved characteristic-zero numerical cap, target construction, general singular-degeneration exclusion, formalization or exponent improvement. Finite controls are not a proof of the all-size statement.
